text.p: Small-scale local initiatives have the potential to create numerous jobs in the service sector if they are given propoer encouragement by the member states and the EU, the European Parliament said on Thursday.

MEPs adopted a report by German Christian Democrat Edgar Schiedermeier which urges the national and European authorities to tackle the legal, fiscal, administrative, financial and training obstacles preventing local job initiatives from flourishing.
"Jobs cannot be wished into existence. They are the result of investment," Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn told MEPs.

He said national and regional policies should concentrate on removing the obstacles. The European Commission could contribute by setting up pilot projects and disseminating information about successful national schemes.
Flynn announced he intended to dedicate 25 million Ecus from the European Social Funds to innovative ways of creating jobs.
